eh4gH0gBQ5Y.title: Advancing Towards the Basics, a Practical Example: Bankruptcy
eh4gH0gBQ5Y.one_line: Using the hadith of the bankrupt, he shows that harming people and breaking trust can zero out all worship, so basics must outrank details.
eh4gH0gBQ5Y.summary: He offers this khutbah as a worked example for his series because listeners were confused. Arguing over tertiary details needs a unity and strength the ummah no longer has, and it leaves logical young people confused, losing respect for their elders or for the faith. He tests the audience: is it that a person without faith cannot be trusted, or that a person without trust has no faith? The hadith says the second, and hesitating shows the problem. There are two ways to fail the test of the Day of Judgment. Everyone preaches the first, denying Allah. The second is ignored: in Al-Muddaththir and Al-Haqqah the people of Hell name failing to feed the needy and going with the crowd beside prayer and belief, and the Quran never gives disbelief as the only reason. The hadith of the bankrupt, whose prayer and fasting are handed to those he harmed, and the martyr punished for a stolen cloak make the same point. In the second khutbah he adds the hadith of deeds turned to dust by private sins, the atom of arrogance, and the Prophet warning that a wrong judgment in someone's favour hands them a piece of Hell. He closes by saying voting was only a small part of advocacy.

outline.heading: Opening
A worked example for a confused audience
outline.gist: Many listeners found the series unclear, so he gives a practical example. When Muslims are caught up in tertiary details the bigger picture is lost, and doing both needs an intellectual, economic and political luxury the ummah lacks.

outline.heading: A luxury we once had
outline.gist: When the ummah was united and ahead in science and economics it could afford to argue details scholars never settled in a thousand years. It cannot now, and the constant emphasis leaves the young in cognitive dissonance.

outline.heading: Logical youth lose respect
outline.gist: An ummah without committed youth goes nowhere. Young people are logical; faced with elders fighting irrationally over hand placement, moon sighting and zakat details, they stop respecting the elders, the faith or both, and come to think the details matter most.

outline.heading: Which phrase is the hadith?
outline.gist: Is the faithless person untrustworthy, or is the untrustworthy person faithless? The hadith says there is no faith without trustworthiness and no religion without keeping covenants; any hesitation shows how long we have argued over what belongs to scholars.

outline.heading: The first way to fail: denying Allah
outline.gist: There are two ways to get a zero on the Day of Judgment. The one everyone agrees on and preaches is denying the One who set the test, or giving Him partners.

outline.heading: The second way, lost in the noise
outline.gist: The other way to fail is rarely mentioned, drowned out by loud arguments over halal meat and fatwas among people unqualified to discuss them.

outline.heading: An answer from inside Hell
outline.gist: The people of Paradise, the only ones not held in pledge for their deeds, ask those in Saqar what brought them there (74:38-42); we are hearing an answer spoken from the midst of the Fire.

outline.heading: The sandwiched answers
outline.gist: Not praying and denying the Day are easy to preach. Between them sit not feeding the needy and going along with whatever was popular without ever taking a stand (74:43-47); Allah would not let us hear them if they did not matter.

outline.heading: 'He did not urge feeding the poor'
outline.gist: Seize him and shackle him (69:30-34): had the verse stopped at 'he did not believe in Allah' it would be easy, but it adds neglect of the needy. Not once does the Quran give disbelief as the only reason for Hell; there is always behaviour, a fundamental we ignore because it hurts.

outline.heading: Who is the bankrupt?
outline.gist: We argue for hours over a fatwa's details, yet the hadith in Muslim settles it: the Prophet asked who the bankrupt is, and the companions answered the one with no money or possessions.

outline.heading: Handed to his victims
outline.gist: The bankrupt of the ummah comes with prayer, fasting and zakat, but he insulted, slandered, cheated, and physically, mentally and socially abused people. They take his good deeds, then their sins are thrown on him and he is cast into the Fire.

outline.heading: Perfect beard, harmful hands
outline.gist: He wonders whether the bankrupt spent hours on his beard, his thobe and the right hat, precise in small details while missing that harming a human being leaves you with nothing.

outline.heading: The martyr and the stolen cloak
outline.gist: Companions congratulated the Prophet on a man killed in battle, and he told them the man was in the Fire over a garment stolen from the spoils. Were the sheikh to say this as his opinion he would be removed from the minbar; why are we not raising children with this clarity?

outline.heading: Not everything weighs the same
outline.gist: Some parts of the deen are far heavier than others, which we could leave undiscussed for now. Unless we grasp that the one who breaks covenants has no religion and the untrustworthy has no faith, we are in trouble.

outline.heading: Interlude
Mountains of deeds turned to dust
outline.gist: Thawban, who devoted himself to serving the Prophet, heard him say that people will come with deeds like the mountains of Tihamah, and Allah will turn them to scattered dust.

outline.heading: They pray at night, and sin when alone
outline.gist: Frightened, Thawban asked who they are. They are like you and pray at night as you do, but whenever only Allah's eye is on them they violate His limits; they left out intention and their inner connection.

outline.heading: An atom of arrogance
outline.gist: Whoever has an atom's weight of arrogance will not enter Paradise. Thinking yourself better than anyone or anything, without Allah ever telling you so, keeps you outside until it is fixed.

outline.heading: We've lost our grasp on the basics
outline.gist: The questions parents and children bring him focus on what matters least, while honesty, decency, kindness, empathy and respect for people's space and dignity are barely considered.

outline.heading: Known by the basics
outline.gist: These are not optional encouragements but critical parts of the deen. The Prophet was known as the most honest, and his companions were described by such fundamentals, Umar by never accepting any falsehood in his judgments.

outline.heading: 'I am only human': the Prophet as judge
outline.gist: If the Prophet ruled in your favour, no court could convince you otherwise, yet he said he was only human and might be swayed by the better speaker, so whatever he wrongly awarded someone was a piece of Hell.

outline.heading: Know what matters most, and teach it
outline.gist: The companions knew what the priorities were; the extras are good but must never obscure them. If you cannot name the principles and values of Islam, learn them so you can teach your children and stop dividing over lesser things.

outline.heading: Voting was one small piece
outline.gist: Most voted, but that is one small piece of advocacy; it does not fix the problem or lift the responsibility from anyone's shoulders.

outline.heading: More people, time and wealth
outline.gist: Keep following what is happening to Muslims elsewhere. If they are to find justice, the work must continue at a different scale, with more young and old willing to give time, effort and wealth to unite the ummah and push just causes.

outline.heading: Otherwise what is the point?
outline.gist: Without this, khutbahs, building masjids and teaching are empty. These fundamental ethics are being denied to many Muslims, and he will keep speaking about them whatever it costs, because nothing ranks above them.

outline.heading: Outro

JJsjbUzUMNQ.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ma'arij, Part 3: Verses 26-44
JJsjbUzUMNQ.one_line: The musallin's code of conduct: lived accountability, healthy fear, guarded sexuality, kept covenants and quality prayer, and the opponents who rush to reject it.
JJsjbUzUMNQ.summary: Islam must be both lived and carried to others, and preaching without practice is the worse failure. He then completes the behavioural portrait of the musallin. Affirming the Day is a behaviour: someone who truly expects to defend every line of his own book lives carefully, and the hadith on Al-Fatiha shows Allah leaving our claim of worship for us to prove. Fear of punishment must stay alive; the companions, who saw the Prophet, still feared, as Umar's last words and his talk with Abu Musa show, and that fear is healthy pressure. Three verses guard sexuality, which he calls precious, delicate and easily corrupted; Islam permits nearly everything yet restricts two things to one door, deity and sexual expression. He warns that Muslims are losing this argument in the West and that capable people in their thirties are not marrying. Then come trusts, covenants and testimonies, starting with the shahadah, and guarding prayer, quality alongside the earlier consistency. Allah asks why opponents rush in groups against a code that would make anyone a good neighbour, says no one enters Paradise unchanged, swears He can replace them, and leaves them to idle talk until the Day.

outline.heading: Represent Islam to yourself and to others
outline.gist: The juz is about representation, which needs both pieces. Islam applied only to yourself is incomplete, since it was designed for dawah: the Quran defines victory as people finding Allah, not conquest.

outline.heading: Preaching without practising is worse
outline.gist: Of the two failures he would rather someone practise without doing dawah than tell others to do what he does not, commanding righteousness and forgetting himself. The right way is both.

outline.heading: Four requirements, then the forms of dawah
outline.gist: The first four surahs set the personal requirements of knowledge, ethics, spirituality and conduct; the rest of the juz shows how dawah works and what fuels it.

outline.heading: Simple, rhythmic surahs: his mother sensed the meaning
outline.gist: His mother, listening to recitation, said she understood little but could tell it was meaningful. Madani passages are long and legal; the Makki surahs to the end are short, rhythmic verses that stay with you.

outline.heading: The challenge: every word irreplaceable
outline.gist: Allah's challenge to bring a surah like it is not about swapping words, which AI could do. Every word is exactly where it must be; a substitute shifts the meaning.

outline.heading: Profound yet artistic
outline.gist: Profound texts are usually dull and catchy ones empty. The Quran is both, and its art is governed by rules: it cannot be recited like ordinary Arabic.

outline.heading: Imitations sound similar but are empty
outline.gist: Musaylimah produced something that sounded like it but had no substance, while a single surah's oaths can take an hour to explain.

outline.heading: Recap: the panicky self
outline.gist: People are halu': unstable from a history of survival, hopeless when 5 per cent of a full cup is lost and selfish when given good. Allah is describing, not chastising.

outline.heading: Claiming to pray brings obligations
outline.gist: The exception is those who start down the path of prayer, a symbol of being Muslim; the same word is a warning at the end of the Quran. Claim it and hopelessness and stinginess must give way to perseverance and gratitude.

outline.heading: Recap: constant devotion and a designated right
outline.gist: They are consistent in whatever they commit to, the struggle of most people, and set aside a right in their wealth for the needy and deprived.

outline.heading: Affirming the Day is a behaviour
outline.gist: These verses describe conduct, not creed: anyone who believes he will be caught and pay behaves differently. Yawm ad-din is the day of accountability.

outline.heading: Could you defend the book you authored?
outline.gist: Picture reading a book you wrote of every choice, time, wealth and youth, and defending it. Saying the shahadah is a claim, and the book either supports it or does not.

outline.heading: 'You alone we worship': a claim left for you to prove
outline.gist: In the hadith in Muslim Allah answers each verse of Al-Fatiha, but at 'You alone we worship' says only that this is between Him and His servant. Read the verses as claims you must prove at every step.

outline.heading: Stealing in front of a police officer
outline.gist: No sane person steals in front of the police; one who does is taken to hospital for a psychiatric consult, not to jail. Claiming belief in resurrection while living carelessly makes as little sense.

outline.heading: Belief as a comforting claim
outline.gist: Saying you believe in accountability earns ethical merit and a high horse; certainty is when it shows in your choices.

outline.heading: Accountability without consequence means nothing
outline.gist: They fear their Lord's punishment, never feeling safe. Much of the Canadian system holds corrupt politicians to account with no consequence; Allah promises both.

outline.heading: Two eyes that saw the Prophet
outline.gist: People who sat with the Prophet and pledged to him did not all make it. When a young man envied al-Miqdad for seeing him, al-Miqdad grew angry: some who saw him daily ended in the Fire.

outline.heading: Umar's deathbed: 'I wish my mother had never borne me'
outline.gist: Every companion lived with fear of consequence for their mistakes. Umar wept, unsure he had kept the covenant; these were the people who carried the message to us.

outline.heading: Umar and Abu Musa: hoping only to break even
outline.gist: Ibn Umar told Abu Musa's son of their fathers' talk: Abu Musa hoped for reward for the dawah after the Prophet, Umar hoped only that it evened out. Abu Musa's son said Umar was wiser.

outline.heading: Healthy fear is motivating fear
outline.gist: A little stress improves performance; fear of not doing enough pushes you closer to Allah and to hold yourself accountable. The first four traits are personal behaviours; then the gears shift.

outline.heading: Guarding their private parts: sexual from birth to death
outline.gist: Three verses on sexual ethics. The Quran speaks plainly: humans are sexual from birth to old age, and the believers protect and preserve this part of themselves.

outline.heading: Precious, delicate, and a fog over judgment
outline.gist: Exposing children to it is a crime with lasting consequences; adults stay confused about it. Bring sexuality into anything and judgment clouds, which is why relationships are hard.

outline.heading: The classical scholars on its fluidity
outline.gist: Books of fiqh after Abu Hanifah speak openly about it; every one he read says a man should not stare long at young boys, showing they understood sexuality as fluid.

outline.heading: Unprotected, it ruins lives; young men too
outline.gist: Like belief and adaptation, sexuality has a biological predisposition yet is fluid. Left unprotected, through abuse or behaviour, it brings misery. Young men must guard it as much as women.

outline.heading: Why three verses on one topic
outline.gist: No other trait in the list gets three verses. Women's instincts seek stability and family; men's raw instinct seeks many partners, and the believer knows that is not how to see his sexuality.

outline.heading: Except with their spouses: not blamed
outline.gist: The only exception is a wife or one whom the right hand possesses, in the historical context of the verses; expressing sexuality there brings no blame.

outline.heading: Everything is open except two things: first, deity
outline.gist: By default everything is permitted, with few exceptions in food and land. Only two areas are restricted to one option, and the first is deity: one God, beyond time, space and any likeness.

outline.heading: Second, sexual expression: one door
outline.gist: Of infinite possible forms of sexual expression only one is accepted, man and woman in marriage, while the world identifies as anything and marries anything.

outline.heading: Zina, murder and the transgressors
outline.gist: Scholars debate whether zina is worse than murder, since it ruins families and leaves children unsupported. Whoever seeks beyond that has crossed the line.

outline.heading: Losing the argument in the West
outline.gist: Muslims are losing the academic, public and practical argument on sexual ethics, unnoticed in their bubbles. Elsewhere these ideas sound absurd, as they did to him in 2010; past a certain point a society cannot return.

outline.heading: Capable singles in their thirties not marrying
outline.gist: He keeps raising it: capable men and women with every box ticked are not even seeking marriage, while where he grew up people with nothing going for them built families. Without families there is no next generation.

outline.heading: Rot is easy, protecting ethics is hard
outline.gist: Corruption spreads like a weed and is counted on to reach Muslims in time. Where it is the norm, step back for your mental, physical and spiritual health.

outline.heading: Keeping trusts and covenants
outline.gist: They are stewards of what they are entrusted with: honest when they speak, faithful to their word and to documents they sign.

outline.heading: Standing by their testimonies: Islam has a buy-in
outline.gist: They stand by what they testify to and advocate. Remember your first testimony, the shahadah: like a golf club, Islam has a buy-in, so see it through. He recaps the list so far.

outline.heading: Guarding their prayer: quality as well as quantity
outline.gist: The word returns so the list cannot be misread. Consistency was about time and devotion; guarding is about doing it well. Few good prayers do not replace many, nor many careless ones a few good.

outline.heading: Connection and trust calm the panicky self
outline.gist: Knowing Allah still sees you and has not forgotten you calms the swinging barometer. He gave once and will give again, so you can afford to give.

outline.heading: Without God, selfishness is the rational way to live
outline.gist: Without belief the world is a scary place: cut every corner and bite first. He cites an obnoxious Levantine saying that praises the one sneaky enough to outsmart others.

outline.heading: Restricted, not shamed

HUgZaiK8_Rc.title: Advancing Towards the Basics: Constants and Variables
HUgZaiK8_Rc.one_line: Using 3:7, he separates Islam's non-negotiable constants from debatable variables and warns that obsessing over variables drives youth away.
HUgZaiK8_Rc.summary: The sheikh says Islam never asked Muslims to invent anything, only to hold on to the fundamentals, yet the ummah is absorbed in variables instead of constants. Aal-Imran 3:7 divides revelation into clear, governing verses that lead, and ambiguous ones that people with diseased hearts chase to win arguments and claim exclusive interpretation. The verse that follows is a dua against hearts deviating, because obsession with variables leads hearts, and the ummah, astray. He swears that the more practising Muslims fight over details like eight or twenty rakahs of taraweeh, the more young people abandon the fundamentals. Values and ethics are not for sale, and some battles, such as speaking openly about gender, are already lost. The remedy is knowledge. A ruling is constant only through its underlying reason, not its benefits: removing the health risks of pork does not make it halal, and medical anaesthesia is not recreational intoxication, so the principle is what Muslims defend and rulings are left to scholars. The hadith of the dishevelled traveller whose dua is rejected for haram income shows the order of priorities, like the worshipper who speeds and parks illegally for Jumuah. He ends by calling for a principled vote in the federal election: voting is a variable, support for Gaza is a constant.

outline.heading: Opening
Islam asks us to hold on, not invent
outline.gist: Muslims were never required to come up with something new, only to hold on to the fundamentals the Prophet taught. The ummah has drifted, absorbed in variables instead of constants.

outline.heading: The clear verses: mother and leader of the Book
outline.gist: In 3:7 the Book is the body of teachings. Its clear, governing verses are the constants no one may debate or issue a fatwa around; 'umm' shares a root with 'imam', the mother who leads her young, so these verses lead and are taken first.

outline.heading: Ambiguous verses and the famous hadith
outline.gist: Other verses resemble each other and are harder to tell apart. The same vocabulary appears in the famous hadith of the clear halal, the clear haram and the doubtful matters between them, so the idea runs through Islam.

outline.heading: Those with deviation chase the ambiguous
outline.gist: People with diseased hearts and personal interests become obsessed with the unclear verses, pursuing disputes and claiming the exclusive right to interpret them. Only Allah knows their full meaning; those firmly grounded say all of it is from our Lord.

outline.heading: 'Let not our hearts deviate'
outline.gist: The dua of 3:8 follows because obsession with variables makes hearts, and the whole ummah, deviate. He swears to the correlation: the more masjid-goers obsess over details, the more the youth abandon the fundamentals.

outline.heading: Principles are not rulings
outline.gist: Principles, values and ethics are a different category from rulings of jurisprudence and are treated differently. They are never for sale; your whole life is holding on to them.

outline.heading: They wish you would compromise
outline.gist: The Prophet was warned repeatedly that his opponents wanted him to give a little so they could give a little (68:9); they held nothing constant. Our job is to stand guard over these values.

outline.heading: Battles already lost
outline.gist: Some things can no longer be said without risking jobs, popularity or the law. One reason is that Muslims are busy fighting over variables that scholars of their own school never agreed on.

outline.heading: Gender: a constant we can no longer speak of
outline.gist: It is hard even to talk about gender, though the parameters were never disputed in Islamic history; meanwhile we argued over eight or twenty rakahs of taraweeh.

outline.heading: Why the youth walk away
outline.gist: Young people watch elders fight over zakat details and parents obsess over haircuts, conclude the religion is not for them, and rarely listen when he tries to explain it is cultural, not core.

outline.heading: The fix is knowledge
outline.gist: Only learning lets you tell what is constant and guarded from what scholars have differed on and you may follow your madhhab in. Muslims can no longer afford not to know their faith.

outline.heading: A ruling's benefits and its reason
outline.gist: Every ruling has something after it, the hikmah or benefits you can list, and something before it, the 'illah, the reason and objective behind it. Pork is his example.

outline.heading: What is constant is the reason
outline.gist: A ruling stands while its reason stands and lapses when it is gone. Pork has no reason given beyond its prohibition; worms and diet are benefits, not the reason.

outline.heading: The clean pig and the anaesthetic
outline.gist: A pig raised on butter and milk and vaccinated is still haram, because removing benefits changes nothing. The reasons come from Islam's principles: recreational intoxication is forbidden, which is why anaesthesia for surgery is permitted.

outline.heading: Defend principles, leave rulings to scholars
outline.gist: The same drug taken recreationally is haram. Muslims defend the principles behind rulings, not the rulings themselves, which are variables whose application belongs to scholars, not laypeople.

outline.heading: Allah is pure and accepts only the pure
outline.gist: The hadith in Muslim states a fundamental: Allah never accepts the haram, so the end never justifies the means and stolen money cannot be given in charity. Believers were commanded what the messengers were (23:51, 2:172).

outline.heading: The dishevelled traveller
outline.gist: A humble-looking traveller raises his hands in dua, but his food and clothes were bought with haram money, so how will he be answered? The maxim is to bring only halal home, even if you go hungry; dress or place of dua are details.

outline.heading: What's the point of the white robe?
outline.gist: He wears white because the Prophet did, but if he lied to patients in his clinic or took what was not his, his dress and eloquence would mean nothing. The next generation must get this right.

outline.heading: Speeding to Jumuah
outline.gist: Coming to Jumuah is good, but speeding, cutting people off, leaving the car where it may not park and shoving through the door to pray shows you missed what matters.

outline.heading: Say 'I believe in Allah', then be upright
outline.gist: Asked for a word about Islam needing no further question, the Prophet said to believe and stand straight. The man who would do only the obligations would succeed if truthful: do the required well and come to Allah with clean hands.

outline.heading: Interlude
The cup and the mother
outline.gist: If a son gets the same slap for dropping a glass of water as for screaming at his mother, he will think the two are equal.

outline.heading: Misrepresenting Islam while the ummah dies
outline.gist: Without knowing the constants we misrepresent Islam, repel people and confuse ourselves, while Muslims are murdered, pulled from rubble and starved and the ummah stays divided.

outline.heading: So the young don't grow up fixated
outline.gist: He has no grievance with anyone; he has watched this since childhood and wants the young to let go of details and focus on the fundamentals.

outline.heading: Vote on principle, not interest
outline.gist: Everyone votes on personal finances; Muslims must vote for those who spoke against the slaughter of Palestinians, so that every politician knows ignoring it costs re-election.

outline.heading: Voting is a variable, Gaza a constant
outline.gist: Voting itself is a variable, but supporting Muslims in Gaza is a constant at the top of the community's priorities, so any action that supports them becomes important.

outline.heading: Find your piece of the puzzle
outline.gist: Give each step its due and do it right, then work out your own piece and what it will cost you. No one will come and pick you up or tell you what to do.

outline.heading: There is hope, if we sort our priorities
outline.gist: He cannot tell people how to support; each must find his way, and together there is hope. It will not come unless we know our constants and give variables less time and argument.

outline.heading: What Islam did: it grounded us
outline.gist: The Prophet brought people back to what matters, and Islam spread quickly and drew the diverse congregation in the room. Every faith suffers when people forget the fundamentals for the details.

outline.heading: Outro

jEZE4o5h8oc.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Honesty, Episode 1
jEZE4o5h8oc.one_line: Launching a tazkiyah series: the four rules (apply to yourself, daily wird, reflection, exercises) and four principles of inner change.
jEZE4o5h8oc.summary: He opens a semi-public tazkiyah series by explaining why such work is normally done in small groups: it consists of exercises that expose how we deal with our own souls, and without follow-up and practice the information only confuses. He lays out four rules. First, everything must be applied to yourself and never projected onto spouses, children or the public; others are constants and only your own nafs is the variable. Second, keep a daily wird twice a day of dhikr, some Quran and dua, because the Prophet stressed remembrance above other voluntary acts, and because obligating yourself to something Allah did not require trains the nafs, which resists new obligations and reveals its hidden priority list when asked to give dhikr its own time. Third, practise focused contemplation, which hurts at first because we prefer to think while distracted; journal and be patient for months. Fourth, do the exercises, such as praying for someone you resent, to learn to recognise the voice of the nafs that only wants immediate, self-serving gain. He then gives four principles: change is gradual, it rests on consistent habits, self-honesty is the pillar without which tazkiyah turns into self-validation, and bad habits must be cut off at once and replaced with an alternative, since fake highs like backbiting dull real emotion.

outline.heading: Opening
Why tazkiyah is taught in close groups

outline.heading: Interlude

outline.gist: Applying tazkiyah to others backfires and makes you worse; others are constants and only your nafs can be changed.

outline.heading: Only mentor those who ask, and beware with your children
outline.gist: You hold others to these concepts only when they invite you to guide them; raising children is not the same as being their spiritual guide.

outline.heading: Rule two: a daily wird twice a day
outline.gist: A fixed amount of dhikr, some Quran and dua, once early and once late in the day, kept as a lifelong covenant.

outline.heading: The Prophet's emphasis on remembrance
outline.gist: He told a man overwhelmed by Islam to keep his tongue moist with dhikr and called it better than spending wealth or fighting.

outline.heading: Starting on the commute is fine
outline.gist: Dhikr can be done while driving or walking at first, though he will later ask for dedicated time.

outline.heading: Giving dhikr its own time exposes the nafs' priorities
outline.gist: Dead time is easy to give; dedicated time is hard because the nafs ranks dhikr low, which is why routines collapse on weekends.

outline.heading: Levels of conviction
outline.gist: Being told something is important is not the same as truly believing it; difficulty with timing reveals the gap.

outline.heading: Add gradually over months
outline.gist: His teachers reached thousands of repetitions with ease because they built up slowly from small amounts.

outline.heading: Why a fixed self-obligation matters
outline.gist: The nafs resists new obligations; binding yourself out of love to what Allah did not require trains it, while an open-ended plan lets it forget.

outline.heading: Rule three: daily contemplation of the topics
outline.gist: You must think about each topic yourself so that you hit the walls he expects and come back with real questions.

outline.heading: Learning by doing, like exam practice
outline.gist: A student who is only handed answers fails; each nafs must be experienced firsthand.

outline.heading: We park thoughts in the back seat
outline.gist: People mull issues over in the background for long periods; this does not work for tazkiyah.

outline.heading: We cannot hold focus
outline.gist: The Prophet reflected for hours; most people manage seconds before another thought intrudes because focus overwhelms them.

outline.heading: Thinking is painful, so we prefer distraction
outline.gist: Like children distracted during vaccination, we avoid deep thought or only think while talking to others.

outline.heading: Journal and be patient
outline.gist: Keep notes of conclusions and expect topics to take months; change shows over a year or two.

outline.heading: Rule four: exercises create reference points
outline.gist: Each task isolates an inner emotion in a safe setting so you recognise it when life brings it.

outline.heading: Praying for someone you resent
outline.gist: The excuses people bring are the nafs speaking, like a child repeating what someone else fed them.

outline.heading: The nafs only does what serves it now
outline.gist: It seeks credit, status and short-term wins and changes only through long purification.

outline.heading: The nafs is like a three-year-old
outline.gist: It cannot grasp delayed reward or death and always wants what is near.

outline.heading: What comes too early ruins people
outline.gist: Most child stars struggle in later life because they received fame long before they could handle it.

outline.heading: The four rules restated
outline.gist: Apply it to yourself, keep the twice-daily wird, contemplate, and do the exercises, or the effort is wasted.

outline.heading: Principle one: change is gradual
outline.gist: Like a child's growth it is only visible across years; harsh sudden change overwhelms the nafs and collapses.

outline.heading: Principle two: build consistent habits
outline.gist: The most beloved deeds to Allah are the consistent ones even if small.

outline.heading: Principle three: self-honesty as a pillar
outline.gist: Without it tazkiyah backfires, turning into arrogance or into validation of one's own choices and mistakes.

outline.heading: The social mask versus the self before Allah
outline.gist: Keep your public image, but before Allah deal with who you really are; rationalising everything makes tazkiyah harmful.

outline.heading: Principle four: cut bad habits off at once
outline.gist: Good habits grow gradually but sins must stop immediately and permanently, as recovering alcoholics know.

outline.heading: Every removed habit needs an alternative
outline.gist: Smokers struggle because the after-meal ritual leaves a gap; something must fill it.

outline.heading: Backbiting gives a drug-like false high
outline.gist: Gossip swings the pendulum toward superiority, and like hard drugs it numbs a person to genuine joys.

outline.heading: Real emotions and your own responsibility
outline.gist: Genuine emotions are less intense but fulfilling; your tazkiyah is your responsibility, he only simplifies the path.

outline.heading: Outro

kC_vGF6SDB4.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Ma'arij, Part 2: Verses 19-28
kC_vGF6SDB4.one_line: The human being is created panicky, despairing in hardship and stingy in ease; the cure is constant connection, a set right for the poor, accountability and healthy fear.
kC_vGF6SDB4.summary: After recapping Juz Tabarak as the requirements for representing Islam, he reads verses 19-21 as a description of human nature, not a rebuke: left untrained, people despair at the slightest harm and clutch what they are given, like a toddler with a cookie. That fretful instinct, built for survival, makes people miserable whether poor or rich, and he urges zooming out, replacing despair with perseverance and stinginess with gratitude and giving. The Prophet mastered this so gracefully it goes unnoticed: he lost eighteen close people, including six children, and still rose each morning. The exceptions are the musallin. Identifying as Muslim is only the start; their prayer is described with a noun sentence, signalling a constant connection with Allah that is the first defence against panic. He adds that addiction and mental illness need professional help. They set a known right in their wealth for the asker and the deprived, seeing their balance as mixed until zakat purifies it, and he recounts Umar's endowed land. Affirming the Day means accepting accountability, and true believers never feel safe from Allah's punishment, a healthy fear that keeps them questioning their choices.

outline.heading: Why every Muslim should know the final juz
outline.gist: Al-Ma'arij is the fourth surah of the cluster in Juz 29. Like a book's closing summary, these short, rhythmic surahs condense nearly every topic the Quran covers, so even those who struggle to memorise should know them.

outline.heading: The requirements of representing Islam
outline.gist: The cluster sets the requirements for anyone carrying Islam: knowledge, ethics, spirituality and behaviour, which today's verses detail. The later surahs give examples of dawah that worked and dawah that did not.

outline.heading: If it stops with you, the job is not done
outline.gist: Finding Islam is not enough; within your capacity you must take it to those around you, by word or by conduct, among colleagues, classmates and neighbours.

outline.heading: Rising levels with no ceiling, and why the surah opens with the Day
outline.gist: Ma'arij are levels one above another: there is no limit to how close you can come to Allah. The opening scenes of isolation and ransom are there to motivate the practices that follow.

outline.heading: Three verses on human nature: recitation
outline.gist: He introduces the three verses that summarise human behaviour and recites them.

outline.heading: Created halu': a description, not a rebuke
outline.gist: Halu', panicky and fretful, describes what instinct produces when left unfiltered and untrained. The verse is not chastising people but describing them.

outline.heading: The thin line between a good day and a bad day
outline.gist: One small negative is enough to ruin a day, though a step back would show positives beyond counting.

outline.heading: Barely touched by harm, despair; touched by good, stinginess
outline.gist: Massa is the least possible contact: the slightest harm makes him feel doomed, and a little good makes him guard it and refuse to share.

outline.heading: The toddler and the cookie
outline.gist: Refuse a toddler a cookie and he melts down; give it and he stuffs it in his face so no one else can touch it. Cute at three, not at thirty: life is rarely all or nothing.

outline.heading: Zoom out and count what is going well
outline.gist: The verses neither chastise nor approve; this is nature left untrained. Every so often step back and say alhamdulillah for what you have, and the problem shrinks.

outline.heading: Little to worry about: life ends and you are soon forgotten
outline.gist: Death is what gives life meaning and urgency. Soon what you have will not matter: heirs sell it in a yard sale, and within decades you are at most a name, as even great scholars are to us.

outline.heading: Constant worry makes life impossible
outline.gist: Life always brings curve balls, and the ways things could go wrong are endless. Obsessing over them blinds you to the small good things: tea with your son, a call, a summer sunset.

outline.heading: Given good, now owned by what you own
outline.gist: When Allah gives, the panicky self becomes obsessed with protecting it. The most prescribed drug in the world is taken largely by the wealthy.

outline.heading: The problem is internal: the nafs loves you but is ignorant
outline.gist: Miserable without and obsessed with, such a person has nothing that can make him happy. The nafs, programmed for survival, is your biggest cheerleader but does not know your interest.

outline.heading: Animals live to survive; humans can reflect
outline.gist: Serengeti mammals run all day to eat or avoid being eaten. Living that way leaves no room for the reflection only humans have; lions do not stargaze.

outline.heading: Perseverance and gratitude in place of despair and stinginess
outline.gist: Allah removes the two states and replaces them, so you can calm down and enjoy a blue and green planet unlike anything in a dark universe of burning stars and dead planets.

outline.heading: Hardship is a chance to prove, ease a chance to share
outline.gist: Do not hate yourself for your nature; retrain it. Hardship is a tax-free chance to prove yourself; when given good, share it. See not the gift but the Giver, whose stores never run dry.

outline.heading: The exceptions, and mastery that goes unnoticed
outline.gist: The next verse gives the exception: people who learned to be better, described by a list of attributes. The Prophet embodied them so gracefully that it goes unnoticed.

outline.heading: Masters make it look easy: his first try at tennis
outline.gist: He critiqued players from the couch, then could not keep a single ball on the court. The Prophet mastered living, so much of his behaviour looks easy until you face the same.

outline.heading: Eighteen bereavements and a smile each morning
outline.gist: Two or three losses traumatise most people. The Prophet lost his parents, grandfather, uncles, Khadijah, Zayd, his children, cousins and servants, eighteen in all, and still rose each morning.

outline.heading: Burying six children
outline.gist: Of his seven children, six died in his lifetime. Parents who lose one never get over it; he wept, mourned and kept going.

outline.heading: Prepared, not expecting the worst
outline.gist: That grace takes practice, reflection and settled values. Live expecting good but prepared for bad; without that, hardship brings jaza' and blessings bring obsession.

outline.heading: Refining your nature gradually
outline.gist: Acknowledge the nature without self-loathing, then slowly trade a little panic for perseverance and a little stinginess for gratitude until the percentages change.

outline.heading: Recitation through verse 35
outline.gist: He recites the full list of attributes to the end of verse 35.

outline.heading: Except the musallin
outline.gist: The exception is those who identify as people of prayer. The same word appears later in the Quran with a negative sense.

outline.heading: Identifying as Muslim is not enough
outline.gist: No verse in the list mentions belief because the basics are assumed. The shahadah benefits you on the Day according to how much you have filled it with action.

outline.heading: Constant in their prayer: a noun sentence
outline.gist: A noun sentence implies permanence where a verb implies renewal, like calling someone a player. Their connection with Allah is constant.

outline.heading: Salah as connection
outline.gist: Salah comes from connecting: an ongoing conversation with Allah. The five prayers ensure a pure connection, kept alive in between.

outline.heading: Attributes sandwiched between two kinds of prayer
outline.gist: The list begins with constancy in prayer and ends with guarding it. The longer you go without remembering Allah, the weaker your grasp of your faith.

outline.heading: The first defence against panic
outline.gist: Trust that comes from connection brings the calm that counters the panicky nature. Many companions lived and died poor and were content, knowing their wealth was with Allah.

outline.heading: Beyond the five: guarding against oblivion
outline.gist: The verse goes beyond the obligatory prayers to a connection that does not lapse. Do not be like those who forgot Allah and were made to forget themselves; connection leaves no room for indecency.

outline.heading: Addiction rewires the brain
outline.gist: Addiction is a different problem: even a fully conscious person cannot stop, so reaching out for professional help is essential.

outline.heading: Mental illness may need professional help first
outline.gist: Conditions like OCD may need treatment or medication before this advice can work. From his psychiatry rotations, much of recovery is a healthy routine of sleep, food and getting out.

outline.heading: A known right for the asker and the deprived
outline.gist: The sa'il makes his need known; the mahrum was never given anything and may not know what to ask for. They set a defined right for both in their wealth.

outline.heading: Two kinds of deeds: salah and zakat as symbols
outline.gist: Some deeds benefit others directly and some do not. The Quran pairs salah and zakat as symbols of the two categories, never fasting, which would be redundant.

outline.heading: Your balance is mixed until zakat purifies it
outline.gist: Look at your bank account as your wealth plus the right of the poor. Zakat, from purification, removes their share so what remains is purely yours.

outline.heading: A right beyond zakat loosens attachment
outline.gist: Most scholars say the defined right goes beyond zakat. Holding a standard of giving beyond 2.5 per cent loosens the strings that make loss and departure agonising.

outline.heading: Give from what you love: Umar's land
outline.gist: You will not attain righteousness until you give what you love. Umar asked what to do with the dearest land he ever owned and endowed it for people to use.

outline.heading: Affirming the Day is a way of behaving
outline.gist: Tasdiq here is behavioural: truly believing in resurrection means accepting that you will be held accountable, and living accordingly.

outline.heading: Din means accountability
outline.gist: At its root din is accountability. Those who accept it watch their steps and have reasons for their choices; pull it out and the whole structure of faith collapses.

outline.heading: Never safe from their Lord's punishment
outline.gist: They live in a state of fear of their Lord's punishment, which no one may feel safe from.

outline.heading: Accountability needs consequences
outline.gist: Accountability only means something if it can lead to punishment, as children who are held to account with no consequence stop caring.

outline.heading: Feeling safe is Shaytan's sign
outline.gist: Even the constant in prayer and generous never feel safe. Feeling safe means Shaytan has set you on the wrong track and left you; the Prophet and companions lived with a healthy, motivating fear.

outline.heading: Outro

lUlqHBuVUPQ.title: Tazkiyah Halaqah: Self-Honesty, Episode 2
lUlqHBuVUPQ.one_line: Completing the tazkiyah framework (daily focuses, methods, pillars, goals) and beginning self-honesty: removing the social mask to see yourself truly.
lUlqHBuVUPQ.summary: He finishes laying out the always-applicable framework of tazkiyah. After recapping the rules and principles, he gives four daily focuses: remembering that every act has an outer and inner layer (ihsan), asking whether you are a good servant of Allah, purifying intention as the first box every deed must tick, and fearing that deeds may not be accepted, a thought that by itself generates most of tazkiyah. He then names four methods: external forces such as teachers, companions and the masjid; internal efforts like reflection; lifestyle change, since late nights, poor sleep and phones make spiritual work impossible, as psychiatrists recognise when they start with a patient's routine; and reinforcement through acts of worship. He lists five pillars: self-value, mortality, self-honesty, sensitivity and etiquette, and frugality, without which knowledge can lead to the fate of the reciter and scholar thrown into the fire. Khushu, consistent ethics and pure tawhid are goals that result from the work, not switches one flips. Turning to self-honesty, he separates honesty with people, honesty with Allah about what one claims to want, and honesty with oneself, which means seeing past the social mask one rightly wears. Those who lie to themselves long enough will even swear falsely to Allah believing they are truthful. The exercise for the week is to describe yourself to yourself honestly, avoiding both flattery and self-loathing.

outline.heading: Opening
Start with what always applies
outline.gist: Every discipline should begin with its always-applicable concepts before situational ones.

outline.heading: Recap of the rules: self, wird, contemplation
outline.gist: Apply it to yourself, reset the wird until consistent and then build it, and journal your reflections.

outline.heading: Exercises, because life is a cruel teacher
outline.gist: Controlled exercises reveal weaknesses and strengths cheaply, letting you learn the voice of the nafs before life slaps you.

outline.heading: Recap of the principles: never lie to yourself
outline.gist: Change is gradual and habit-based; you are never asked to deceive yourself; a repented sin needs a replacement.

outline.heading: Daily focus one: the inner layer of every act (ihsan)
outline.gist: Each act has a visible and a spiritual side, and Allah judges the spiritual one.

outline.heading: Daily focus two: am I a good servant?
outline.gist: Servitude is your job description; ask daily whether your choices reflect it, even in how you treat a patient.

outline.heading: Daily focus three: purifying intention
outline.gist: Intention is the first check box; if it fails, every other correct detail is wasted.

outline.heading: Daily focus four: will my deeds be accepted?
outline.gist: Deeds are worth nothing if rejected; contemplating acceptance alone generates most of tazkiyah.

outline.heading: Method one: external forces
outline.gist: Lessons, good companions and the masjid are needed; tazkiyah cannot be done alone or in an indifferent environment.

outline.heading: From Jibril to the Prophet to the companions
outline.gist: Even the Prophet was transformed by an external force, and he then became that force for others.

outline.heading: Method two: internal efforts
outline.gist: Reflection, recitation and the thought-emotion-behaviour cycle need skill; cutting harmful apps is a simple decision, not a tazkiyah topic.

outline.heading: Method three: lifestyle change
outline.gist: If you cannot reach Fajr at the masjid once a weekend, fix sleep, eating, exercise and routine first.

outline.heading: Life without electricity
outline.gist: Where he taught before, power cuts sent everyone to bed early, which kept routines healthy.

outline.heading: Late nights catch up with you
outline.gist: He sees red-eyed colleagues who slept at two; the habit is unsustainable and harms the heart.

outline.heading: Psychiatry starts with your daily routine
outline.gist: Before medication, clinicians fix sleep, waking, showering and walking, because bad routines underlie much distress.

outline.heading: Method four: reinforcement through worship
outline.gist: Ideas sink in only when reinforced repeatedly over months.

outline.heading: The five pillars take years
outline.gist: These foundations usually take two years; his groups have covered barely one and a half in three years.

outline.heading: The five pillars named
outline.gist: Self-value, mortality, self-honesty, sensitivity and etiquette, and frugality and asceticism.

outline.heading: Without the pillars knowledge can damn you
outline.gist: The reciter, scholar and martyr thrown into the fire lacked these foundations; he begins with self-honesty to avoid repetition.

outline.heading: The tools of tazkiyah
outline.gist: The thought-emotion-action cycle, contemplation, exercises, salah step by step, tawbah and striving.

outline.heading: Goals are results: khushu
outline.gist: Khushu cannot be performed on command, like muscles cannot pop without years at the gym.

outline.heading: Goals: consistent ethics and pure tawhid
outline.gist: Ethics held only when convenient must become consistent, and tawhid must be pure in understanding and lifestyle.

outline.heading: Interlude
Ask second-level questions
outline.gist: Think a problem through yourself and come when you hit a wall, rather than asking whatever first comes to mind.

outline.heading: Honesty with people
outline.gist: The simplest domain: truthfulness with others, by which one is recorded with Allah as truthful or a liar.

outline.heading: Honesty with Allah
outline.gist: How truly you want what you ask for; seeking knowledge and effort show your request is sincere.

outline.heading: Honesty with yourself and the social mask
outline.gist: Everyone presents a social identity, which is right and should not be dropped in public.

outline.heading: Your father alone with himself
outline.gist: To you he is your father, but self-honesty means seeing yourself without the role; we come to believe our own constructs.

outline.heading: Believing your own status
outline.gist: Over time we accept the respect and status others give us, though Allah sees us as we are.

outline.heading: Seeing the real you
outline.gist: Privately see the lost, weak, sinful self and question your motives, or every lesson only reinforces existing beliefs.

30:3.ar: فِيٓ أَدۡنَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ غَلَبِهِمۡ سَيَغۡلِبُونَ
30:3.en: In the nearer land, and they, after their defeat will be victorious

30:4.ar: فِي بِضۡعِ سِنِينَۗ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ مِن قَبۡلُ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدُۚ وَيَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَفۡرَحُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
30:4.en: Within ten years - Allah's is the command in the former case and in the latter - and in that day believers will rejoice

30:5.ar: بِنَصۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ يَنصُرُ مَن يَشَآءُۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
30:5.en: In Allah's help to victory. He helpeth to victory whom He will. He is the Mighty, the Merciful

30:6.ar: وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِۖ لَا يُخۡلِفُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:6.en: It is a promise of Allah. Allah faileth not His promise, but most of mankind know not

30:7.ar: يَعۡلَمُونَ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
30:7.en: They know only some appearance of the life of the world, and are heedless of the Hereafter

30:8.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُواْ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۗ مَّا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۗ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِلِقَآيِٕ رَبِّهِمۡ لَكَٰفِرُونَ
30:8.en: Have they not pondered upon themselves? Allah created not the heavens and the earth, and that which is between them, save with truth and for a destined end. But truly many of mankind are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord

2:143.ar: وَكَذَٰلِكَ جَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أُمَّةࣰ وَسَطࣰ ا لِّتَكُونُواْ شُهَدَآءَ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ شَهِيدࣰ اۗ وَمَا جَعَلۡنَا ٱلۡقِبۡلَةَ ٱلَّتِي كُنتَ عَلَيۡهَآ إِلَّا لِنَعۡلَمَ مَن يَتَّبِعُ ٱلرَّسُولَ مِمَّن يَنقَلِبُ عَلَىٰ عَقِبَيۡهِۚ وَإِن كَانَتۡ لَكَبِيرَةً إِلَّا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَدَى ٱللَّهُۗ وَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيُضِيعَ إِيمَٰنَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِٱلنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:143.en: Thus We have appointed you a middle nation, that ye may be witnesses against mankind, and that the messenger may be a witness against you. And We appointed the qiblah which ye formerly observed only that We might know him who followeth the messenger, from him who turneth on his heels. In truth it was a hard (test) save for those whom Allah guided. But it was not Allah's purpose that your faith should be in vain, for Allah is Full of Pity, Merciful toward mankind

3:165.ar: أَوَلَمَّآ أَصَٰبَتۡكُم مُّصِيبَةࣱ قَدۡ أَصَبۡتُم مِّثۡلَيۡهَا قُلۡتُمۡ أَنَّىٰ هَٰذَاۖ قُلۡ هُوَ مِنۡ عِندِ أَنفُسِكُمۡۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
3:165.en: And was it so, when a disaster smote you, though ye had smitten (them with a disaster) twice (as great), that ye said: How is this? Say (unto them, O Muhammad): It is from yourselves. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

3:166.ar: وَمَآ أَصَٰبَكُمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِ فَبِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
3:166.en: That which befell you, on the day when the two armies met, was by permission of Allah; that He might know the true believers

3:167.ar: وَلِيَعۡلَمَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَافَقُواْۚ وَقِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ قَٰتِلُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أَوِ ٱدۡفَعُواْۖ قَالُواْ لَوۡ نَعۡلَمُ قِتَالࣰ ا لَّٱتَّبَعۡنَٰكُمۡۗ هُمۡ لِلۡكُفۡرِ يَوۡمَئِذٍ أَقۡرَبُ مِنۡهُمۡ لِلۡإِيمَٰنِۚ يَقُولُونَ بِأَفۡوَٰهِهِم مَّا لَيۡسَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا يَكۡتُمُونَ
3:167.en: And that He might know the hypocrites, unto whom it was said: Come, fight in the way of Allah, or defend yourselves. They answered: If we knew aught of fighting we would follow you. On that day they were nearer disbelief than faith. They utter with their mouths a thing which is not in their hearts. Allah is Best Aware of what they hide

3:126.ar: وَمَا جَعَلَهُ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بُشۡرَىٰ لَكُمۡ وَلِتَطۡمَئِنَّ قُلُوبُكُم بِهِۦۗ وَمَا ٱلنَّصۡرُ إِلَّا مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡحَكِيمِ
3:126.en: Allah ordained this only as a message of good cheer for you, and that thereby your hearts might be at rest - Victory cometh only from Allah, the Mighty, the Wise

60:8.ar: لَّا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمۡ يُخۡرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمۡ وَتُقۡسِطُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُقۡسِطِينَ
60:8.en: Allah forbiddeth you not those who warred not against you on account of religion and drove you not out from your homes, that ye should show them kindness and deal justly with them. Lo! Allah loveth the just dealers

60:9.ar: إِنَّمَا يَنۡهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَٰتَلُوكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخۡرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمۡ وَظَٰهَرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ إِخۡرَاجِكُمۡ أَن تَوَلَّوۡهُمۡۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُمۡ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
60:9.en: Allah forbiddeth you only those who warred against you on account of religion and have driven you out from your homes and helped to drive you out, that ye make friends of them. Whosoever maketh friends of them - (All) such are wrong-doers

8:65.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ حَرِّضِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ عَلَى ٱلۡقِتَالِۚ إِن يَكُن مِّنكُمۡ عِشۡرُونَ صَٰبِرُونَ يَغۡلِبُواْ مِاْئَتَيۡنِۚ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُم مِّاْئَةࣱ يَغۡلِبُوٓاْ أَلۡفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِأَنَّهُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ لَّا يَفۡقَهُونَ
8:65.en: O Prophet! Exhort the believers to fight. If there be of you twenty steadfast they shall overcome two hundred, and if there be of you a hundred (steadfast) they shall overcome a thousand of those who disbelieve, because they (the disbelievers) are a folk without intelligence

8:66.ar: ٱلۡـَٰٔنَ خَفَّفَ ٱللَّهُ عَنكُمۡ وَعَلِمَ أَنَّ فِيكُمۡ ضَعۡفࣰ اۚ فَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُم مِّاْئَةࣱ صَابِرَةࣱ يَغۡلِبُواْ مِاْئَتَيۡنِۚ وَإِن يَكُن مِّنكُمۡ أَلۡفࣱ يَغۡلِبُوٓاْ أَلۡفَيۡنِ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
8:66.en: Now hath Allah lightened your burden, for He knoweth that there is weakness in you. So if there be of you a steadfast hundred they shall overcome two hundred, and if there be of you a thousand (steadfast) they shall overcome two thousand by permission of Allah. Allah is with the steadfast

2:249.ar: فَلَمَّا فَصَلَ طَالُوتُ بِٱلۡجُنُودِ قَالَ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ مُبۡتَلِيكُم بِنَهَرࣲ فَمَن شَرِبَ مِنۡهُ فَلَيۡسَ مِنِّي وَمَن لَّمۡ يَطۡعَمۡهُ فَإِنَّهُۥ مِنِّيٓ إِلَّا مَنِ ٱغۡتَرَفَ غُرۡفَةَۢ بِيَدِهِۦۚ فَشَرِبُواْ مِنۡهُ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنۡهُمۡۚ فَلَمَّا جَاوَزَهُۥ هُوَ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥ قَالُواْ لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ بِجَالُوتَ وَجُنُودِهِۦۚ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَظُنُّونَ أَنَّهُم مُّلَٰقُواْ ٱللَّهِ كَم مِّن فِئَةࣲ قَلِيلَةٍ غَلَبَتۡ فِئَةࣰ كَثِيرَةَۢ بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ مَعَ ٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ
2:249.en: And when Saul set out with the army, he said: Lo! Allah will try you by (the ordeal of) a river. Whosoever therefore drinketh thereof he is not of me, and whosoever tasteth it not he is of me, save him who taketh (thereof) in the hollow of his hand. But they drank thereof, all save a few of them. And after he had crossed (the river), he and those who believed with him, they said: We have no power this day against Goliath and his hosts. But those who knew that they would meet Allah exclaimed: How many a little company hath overcome a mighty host by Allah's leave! Allah is with the steadfast

9:25.ar: لَقَدۡ نَصَرَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي مَوَاطِنَ كَثِيرَةࣲ وَيَوۡمَ حُنَيۡنٍ إِذۡ أَعۡجَبَتۡكُمۡ كَثۡرَتُكُمۡ فَلَمۡ تُغۡنِ عَنكُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَضَاقَتۡ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ بِمَا رَحُبَتۡ ثُمَّ وَلَّيۡتُم مُّدۡبِرِينَ
9:25.en: Allah hath given you victory on many fields and on the day of Huneyn, when ye exulted in your multitude but it availed you naught, and the earth, vast as it is, was straitened for you; then ye turned back in flight

21:20.en: They glorify (Him) night and day; they flag not

28:79.ar: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فِي زِينَتِهِۦۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا يَٰلَيۡتَ لَنَا مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
28:79.en: Then went he forth before his people in his pomp. Those who were desirous of the life of the world said: Ah, would that we had the like of what hath been given unto Korah! Lo! he is lord of rare good fortune

28:80.ar: وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡعِلۡمَ وَيۡلَكُمۡ ثَوَابُ ٱللَّهِ خَيۡرࣱ لِّمَنۡ ءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ اۚ وَلَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلصَّٰبِرُونَ
28:80.en: But those who had been given knowledge said: Woe unto you! The reward of Allah for him who believeth and doeth right is better, and only the steadfast will obtain it

28:81.ar: فَخَسَفۡنَا بِهِۦ وَبِدَارِهِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ فَمَا كَانَ لَهُۥ مِن فِئَةࣲ يَنصُرُونَهُۥ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَمَا كَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُنتَصِرِينَ
28:81.en: So We caused the earth to swallow him and his dwelling-place. Then he had no host to help him against Allah, nor was he of those who can save themselves

28:82.ar: وَأَصۡبَحَ ٱلَّذِينَ تَمَنَّوۡاْ مَكَانَهُۥ بِٱلۡأَمۡسِ يَقُولُونَ وَيۡكَأَنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَقۡدِرُۖ لَوۡلَآ أَن مَّنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا لَخَسَفَ بِنَاۖ وَيۡكَأَنَّهُۥ لَا يُفۡلِحُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ
28:82.en: And morning found those who had coveted his place but yesterday crying: Ah, welladay! Allah enlargeth the provision for whom He will of His slaves and straiteneth it (for whom He will). If Allah had not been gracious unto us He would have caused it to swallow us (also). Ah, welladay! the disbelievers never prosper

3:141.ar: وَلِيُمَحِّصَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَيَمۡحَقَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
3:141.en: And that Allah may prove those who believe, and may blight the disbelievers

cu1f0aKvMoU.title: Friday Arabic Tafsir: Surat Ar-Rum (Part 2), Verses 1-8
cu1f0aKvMoU.one_line: Ar-Rum 1-8: we know ourselves through relationships, victory follows Allah's laws not labels, quality over numbers, and the danger of knowing only life's surface.
cu1f0aKvMoU.summary: Resuming Ar-Rum, he argues that humans understand their own existence only through relationships, using the deaf child who never acquires language, and that this surah concerns our relationship with Allah's laws. He distinguishes the meanings of the word sunnah across fiqh, usul, hadith and the Quran, where it means Allah's laws, including balance and the rule that excess turns into its opposite. Reviewing the Roman defeat, Abu Bakr's wager and the later Roman victory, he insists Allah does not favour a people for a label: a just unbelieving nation can prevail and an unjust Muslim one fall, as Uhud and Hunayn showed. Muslims may rejoice at the victory of non-Muslims who are friendly to them, with loyalty withheld only from those who fight or expel them. Numbers mean nothing without quality; the Prophet built on a small, sound nucleus and companions worked tirelessly. Unity is only a first step; morals, knowledge and justice must follow. On verses 7-8 he criticizes those who know only the surface of life, who are blind to their own faults, and who never reflect that the world was created with truth and an appointed end. He urges young people to see the effort behind success, ignore empty influencers, master worldly life, and pass this wisdom on.

outline.heading: Opening
We know ourselves only through relationships
outline.gist: The surahs from Al-Qasas to As-Sajdah address the relationships people form; the heart grasps its own existence through them.

outline.heading: The deaf child and the role of language
outline.gist: A deaf child without language by seven fails to mature mentally while a blind child does not, because language builds relationships.

outline.heading: An immature heart cannot read danger
outline.gist: A child walks in front of a train because he has not formed a relationship with the laws around him; Ar-Rum concerns that relationship.

outline.heading: Laws of rising and falling, not physics
outline.gist: Ar-Rum speaks of the laws of victory, revival, success and failure that Muslims must master, unlike Al-Ankabut's focus on enduring life.

outline.heading: Four meanings of the word sunnah
outline.gist: In fiqh a recommended act, in usul a source of law, in hadith the Prophet's words and deeds, and in the Quran Allah's laws.

outline.heading: Created with truth: the law of balance
outline.gist: A world built on truth collapses under falsehood; science only discovers Allah's laws, such as excess turning into its opposite.

outline.heading: No one defeats Allah's laws
outline.gist: Even those without religion see that deeds return to their doers and call it karma; Muslims know these are Allah's laws and honour them.

outline.heading: The Romans defeated in the nearest land
outline.gist: Muslims grieved because the Christian Romans were closer to them than the dualist Persians; most scholars treat Magians as having a scripture.

outline.heading: A crushing defeat and a promise within a few years
outline.gist: Over a hundred thousand Romans died, making the promise of reversal seem impossible; bid' means three to nine.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr's wager and his lawful wealth
outline.gist: Quraysh spread news of his lost six-year bet; the seventh-year victory brought many into Islam and spared Abu Bakr unlawful gain.

outline.heading: No favouritism in Allah's laws
outline.gist: The surah prepared Makkan Muslims for future battles: Allah supports a just unbelieving nation and forsakes an unjust Muslim one.

outline.heading: Uhud: it is from yourselves
outline.gist: The Ansar asked where the angels were, but early companions understood that an army that disobeys its commander loses.

outline.heading: Believers rejoice at Allah's help
outline.gist: Most say joy at the Roman victory, some at Badr; rejoicing at the success of friendly non-Muslims is natural.

outline.heading: Loyalty between two extremes
outline.gist: Muslims may ally with and trust non-Muslims who keep their covenants; loyalty is forbidden only to those who fight, persecute or expel them.

outline.heading: Khosrow's envoys and Badhan of Yemen
outline.gist: The Prophet told Khosrow's envoys their lord had been killed; Persia tore itself apart and its Yemen governor accepted Islam and kept his post.

outline.heading: He gives victory to whom He wills: not arbitrary
outline.gist: Allah supports those committed to their cause and covenants; adding tawhid to these laws earns special support.

outline.heading: The special ratios for steadfast believers
outline.gist: Twenty patient believers overcoming two hundred, then lightened; small groups overcoming large ones, if they fulfil every law.

outline.heading: Uhud: forty men out of seven hundred
outline.gist: A breach by a small fraction cost the Prophet's wounds and the lives of Hamza and Mus'ab.

outline.heading: Hunayn: when numbers impressed you
outline.gist: Trusting their large numbers, they forgot the laws and the earth closed in on them.

outline.heading: Numbers mean nothing: foam on the flood
outline.gist: Overflowing Friday and Eid prayers achieve nothing by themselves; eleven players matter, not a million fans.

outline.heading: Quality over quantity
outline.gist: Twenty-five people with understanding, education and vision move the world; the Prophet built on a small sound nucleus.

outline.heading: Allah's promise: no one stays on top
outline.gist: Days alternate, and Allah will not grant victory to a fearful, sleeping, divided ummah.

outline.heading: Companions who worked without tiring
outline.gist: Like the angels who glorify night and day without flagging, they gave everything and grew more devoted after his death.

outline.heading: Abu Ayyub at ninety
outline.gist: He asked to be carried to the farthest front and buried there, now near Istanbul.

outline.heading: Gathering is only the first step
outline.gist: Victory is not owed for being Muslim; stop killing each other, remove racism and bad customs, then fix morals and learning.

outline.heading: Allah's law is to destroy the corrupt, not support them
outline.gist: If an ignorant, divided, immoral ummah won, the laws would be broken.

outline.heading: Salahuddin and the long preparation
outline.gist: Generations of scholars and fighters prepared before Jerusalem was freed; not everyone must be righteous, but a committed core must exist.

outline.heading: Interlude
They know only the surface of worldly life
outline.gist: Two levels of understanding life: surface and depth; many fail even in their own lives because of shallow understanding.

outline.heading: Blind to our own faults
outline.gist: As Imam al-Haddad noted, we tolerate our own inner filth as we do our physical filth while finding others' repulsive.

outline.heading: Three kinds of understanding
outline.gist: Some unbelievers grasp life's depth but neglect the Hereafter; worst are those who know only its surface.

outline.heading: Reflect within yourselves: truth and an appointed term
outline.gist: Even without revelation, reflection shows that liars and oppressors fail and everything ends.

outline.heading: Qarun's wealth and the shallow onlookers
outline.gist: Those who envied Qarun changed their view once the earth swallowed him.

outline.heading: A fleeting world is not worth lying for
outline.gist: Life is a few orbits of the sun; tyrants end cursed and their families ruined.

outline.heading: Time exposes what we claim to believe
outline.gist: Many claim belief in meeting Allah until it costs them; politicians believe only in their pockets; Allah purifies the believers.

outline.heading: Young people see the goal, not the effort
outline.gist: A footballer trains for years before his moment; youth see only the celebration.

outline.heading: Empty influencers and neglected thinkers
outline.gist: Millions follow hollow content while scholars and thinkers draw a few hundred, though knowledge is now a tap away.

outline.heading: Skills without value: Harun al-Rashid's verdict
outline.gist: Hadith scholars travelled for a single narration; a man who mastered a useless trick was punished for wasting his youth.

outline.heading: Success requires sacrifice
outline.gist: Allah's law is that nothing is achieved without effort; the Prophet devoted every moment to his message.

outline.heading: Youth wasting nights in cafes
outline.gist: At least master worldly life even before the Hereafter; one who loses the world thinking he has won the Hereafter is deluded.

outline.heading: Religion must act in reality
outline.gist: We separate what cannot be separated; the religion must shape life outside the masjid, or others shape the world and we complain.

outline.heading: Pass the wisdom to the next generation
outline.gist: A generation that sees its shortcomings must at least hand the lesson on.

outline.heading: Outro

30:9.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَيَنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ كَانُوٓاْ أَشَدَّ مِنۡهُمۡ قُوَّةࣰ وَأَثَارُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَعَمَرُوهَآ أَكۡثَرَ مِمَّا عَمَرُوهَا وَجَآءَتۡهُمۡ رُسُلُهُم بِٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتِۖ فَمَا كَانَ ٱللَّهُ لِيَظۡلِمَهُمۡ وَلَٰكِن كَانُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ يَظۡلِمُونَ
30:9.en: Have they not travelled in the land and seen the nature of the consequence for those who were before them? They were stronger than these in power, and they dug the earth and built upon it more than these have built. Messengers of their own came unto them with clear proofs (of Allah's Sovereignty). Surely Allah wronged them not, but they did wrong themselves

30:10.ar: ثُمَّ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَٰٓـُٔواْ ٱلسُّوٓأَىٰٓ أَن كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَكَانُواْ بِهَا يَسۡتَهۡزِءُونَ
30:10.en: Then evil was the consequence to those who dealt in evil, because they denied the revelations of Allah and made a mock of them

30:11.ar: ٱللَّهُ يَبۡدَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ ثُمَّ إِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
30:11.en: Allah produceth creation, then He reproduceth it, then unto Him ye will be returned

30:12.en: And in the day when the Hour riseth the unrighteous will despair

30:13.ar: وَلَمۡ يَكُن لَّهُم مِّن شُرَكَآئِهِمۡ شُفَعَٰٓؤُاْ وَكَانُواْ بِشُرَكَآئِهِمۡ كَٰفِرِينَ
30:13.en: There will be none to intercede for them of those whom they made equal with Allah. And they will reject their partners (whom they ascribed unto Him)

30:14.en: In the day when the Hour cometh, in that day they will be sundered

30:15.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ فَهُمۡ فِي رَوۡضَةࣲ يُحۡبَرُونَ
30:15.en: As for those who believed and did good works, they will be made happy in a Garden

30:16.ar: وَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ وَكَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا وَلِقَآيِٕ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ٱلۡعَذَابِ مُحۡضَرُونَ
30:16.en: But as for those who disbelieved and denied Our revelations, and denied the meeting of the Hereafter, such will be brought to doom

30:3.ar: فِيٓ أَدۡنَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ غَلَبِهِمۡ سَيَغۡلِبُونَ
30:3.en: In the nearer land, and they, after their defeat will be victorious

30:4.ar: فِي بِضۡعِ سِنِينَۗ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ مِن قَبۡلُ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدُۚ وَيَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَفۡرَحُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
30:4.en: Within ten years - Allah's is the command in the former case and in the latter - and in that day believers will rejoice

30:5.ar: بِنَصۡرِ ٱللَّهِۚ يَنصُرُ مَن يَشَآءُۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
30:5.en: In Allah's help to victory. He helpeth to victory whom He will. He is the Mighty, the Merciful

30:6.ar: وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِۖ لَا يُخۡلِفُ ٱللَّهُ وَعۡدَهُۥ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَ ٱلنَّاسِ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
30:6.en: It is a promise of Allah. Allah faileth not His promise, but most of mankind know not

30:7.ar: يَعۡلَمُونَ ظَٰهِرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ هُمۡ غَٰفِلُونَ
30:7.en: They know only some appearance of the life of the world, and are heedless of the Hereafter

30:8.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَتَفَكَّرُواْ فِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۗ مَّا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَآ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَأَجَلࣲ مُّسَمࣰّ ىۗ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ بِلِقَآيِٕ رَبِّهِمۡ لَكَٰفِرُونَ
30:8.en: Have they not pondered upon themselves? Allah created not the heavens and the earth, and that which is between them, save with truth and for a destined end. But truly many of mankind are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord

28:83.ar: تِلۡكَ ٱلدَّارُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ نَجۡعَلُهَا لِلَّذِينَ لَا يُرِيدُونَ عُلُوࣰّ ا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا فَسَادࣰ اۚ وَٱلۡعَٰقِبَةُ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
28:83.en: As for that Abode of the Hereafter We assign it unto those who seek not oppression in the earth, nor yet corruption. The sequel is for those who ward off (evil)

48:29.ar: مُّحَمَّدࣱ رَّسُولُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ تَرَىٰهُمۡ رُكَّعࣰ ا سُجَّدࣰ ا يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ اۖ سِيمَاهُمۡ فِي وُجُوهِهِم مِّنۡ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِۚ ذَٰلِكَ مَثَلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِۚ وَمَثَلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡإِنجِيلِ كَزَرۡعٍ أَخۡرَجَ شَطۡـَٔهُۥ فَـَٔازَرَهُۥ فَٱسۡتَغۡلَظَ فَٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِۦ يُعۡجِبُ ٱلزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ ٱلۡكُفَّارَۗ وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِنۡهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣰ وَأَجۡرًا عَظِيمَۢا
48:29.en: Muhammad is the messenger of Allah. And those with him are hard against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. Thou (O Muhammad) seest them bowing and falling prostrate (in worship), seeking bounty from Allah and (His) acceptance. The mark of them is on their foreheads from the traces of prostration. Such is their likeness in the Torah and their likeness in the Gospel - like as sown corn that sendeth forth its shoot and strengtheneth it and riseth firm upon its stalk, delighting the sowers - that He may enrage the disbelievers with (the sight of) them. Allah hath promised, unto such of them as believe and do good works, forgiveness and immense reward

11:117.ar: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ لِيُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ بِظُلۡمࣲ وَأَهۡلُهَا مُصۡلِحُونَ
11:117.en: In truth thy Lord destroyed not the townships tyrannously while their folk were doing right

17:37.ar: وَلَا تَمۡشِ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَحًاۖ إِنَّكَ لَن تَخۡرِقَ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ وَلَن تَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡجِبَالَ طُولࣰ ا
17:37.en: And walk not in the earth exultant. Lo! thou canst not rend the earth, nor canst thou stretch to the height of the hills

76:1.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ حِينࣱ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهۡرِ لَمۡ يَكُن شَيۡـࣰٔ ا مَّذۡكُورًا
76:1.en: Hath there come upon man (ever) any period of time in which he was a thing unremembered

10:102.ar: فَهَلۡ يَنتَظِرُونَ إِلَّا مِثۡلَ أَيَّامِ ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡۚ قُلۡ فَٱنتَظِرُوٓاْ إِنِّي مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُنتَظِرِينَ
10:102.en: What expect they save the like of the days of those who passed away before them? Say: Expect then! I am with you among the expectant
